body.statement:
For a first-order formula over a real closed field whose atoms are polynomial
sign conditions with integer coefficients, effective quantifier elimination
terminates, produces an equivalent quantifier-free formula, and can produce
real-algebraic sample points for every nonempty sign condition.  With a fixed
number of quantifier blocks, the bit complexity and the degrees and coefficient
heights of the resulting algebraic representations are bounded by the input
bit length raised to an exponent polynomial in the block dimensions; exact
arithmetic and sign determination at the represented real-algebraic points are
effective within the same singly-exponential-in-dimension envelope.

source.locator: Theorem 13.11, p. 514 (algebraic sampling and representation bounds), and Theorem 14.16, pp. 550--551 (the displayed fixed-block quantifier-elimination complexity, output-size, degree, and integer-bitsize bounds)
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 13.11. Let P be a set of s polynomials each of degree at most d in k variables with coefficients in a real closed field R. Let D be the ring generated by the coefficients of P. There is an algorithm that computes a set of points meeting every semi-algebraically connected component of the realization of every realizable sign condition on P in R⟨ε, δ⟩^k. There is also an algorithm computing the signs of all the polynomials in P at each of these points. The degrees of the univariate representations output are bounded by O(d)^k. If the polynomials in P have coefficients in Z of bitsizes at most τ, the bitsizes of the coefficients of these univariate representations are bounded by τd^{O(k)}. Theorem 14.16. [Quantifier Elimination] Let P be a set of at most s polynomials each of degree at most d in k plus ell variables with coefficients in a real closed field R, and let Pi denote a partition into blocks of sizes k_i. Given Phi(Y), a (P,Pi)-formula, there exists an equivalent quantifier-free formula Psi(Y). Moreover, the displayed complexity is s raised to the product of (k_i+1), times (ell+1), times d raised to the product of O(k_i) and O(ell); for integer coefficients of bitsize tau, the intermediate and output bitsizes are bounded by tau times the same d factor.

attestation.note: Theorem 13.11 is transcribed verbatim from the second-edition PDF posted on coauthor Saugata Basu’s Purdue homepage (bpr-ed2.pdf), printed p. 514; Theorem 14.16's parameter-by-parameter displayed bound is transcribed from printed pp. 550–551. Retrieved 2026-09-07; products, subscripts, and broken PDF lineation are normalized.
